lessons.sourceTitleEnglish: Mediate Two Friends' Pre-Trek Breakfast Argument
lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Report each friend's position fairly, add the staff's facts, and help the group agree on one plan.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: You are the friend in the middle, and the AI plays Ana, Lars and Wilber from the hostel: report each friend's position fairly with dijo que and decía que plus the imperfect, add Wilber's facts about the market, and help everyone agree on one plan.
lessons.sourceGrammarFocusEnglish: Reported speech; imperfect for background (Ana dijo que quería ir al mercado; Lars decía que no había tiempo)

sourceWordsEnglish.en: Ana said she wanted to try the hen broth at the market.
Lars was saying there wasn't time before the pickup.
Wilber, could you tell me what time the market opens?
Wilber explained to us that the market opened at 6.
Listen, you both have a point.
Lars, you were saying the pickup was at 7, right?
What if we go to the market and come back before 7?
So it's settled: a quick market trip and backpacks ready beforehand.

sourcePassageEnglish: It was 5 in the early morning in Cusco, and my friends Ana and Lars were arguing before the trek.
We were in the hostel kitchen, where Wilber, the person in charge, was making a hot emoliente.
Ana said she wanted to try the hen broth at the market.
She was also saying that the chuta bread at the San Pedro market was famous and that she didn't want to leave Cusco without trying it.
Lars was saying there wasn't time before the pickup.
His position was that the hostel's quinoa was enough and that rushing around with altitude sickness before a long trek was a bad idea.
I stepped into the middle and told them: Listen, you both have a point.
Then I asked Lars: Lars, you were saying the pickup was at 7, right?
Lars checked the agency's message and confirmed that the pickup time was at 7 at the hostel door.
Then I asked Wilber: Wilber, could you tell me what time the market opens?
Wilber explained to us that the market opened at 6.
He added that, after the opening, the broth stalls filled up quickly and that the market was a 10-minute walk away.
Wilber also said that coca tea helped many travelers with altitude sickness, so he served each of us a cup.
With that information, I proposed a middle ground: What if we go to the market and come back before 7?
Ana agreed to come back at 6:45, and Lars said he was on board if we left our backpacks ready at the front desk.
To close the agreement, I summed it up out loud: So it's settled: a quick market trip and backpacks ready beforehand.
Ana smiled, Lars finished his emoliente, and we headed out to San Pedro at 6 sharp.

sourceVerbsEnglish.exampleEnglish: Lars says there isn't time before the pickup.
Ana wants to try the hen broth at the market.
Wilber explains that the market opens at 6.
We come back to the hostel before 7.

sourceVerbsEnglish.meaningEnglish: to agree on, to settle (a plan); to be located
sourceVerbsEnglish.exampleEnglish: So it's settled: a quick market trip and backpacks ready beforehand.

sourceGrammarExamplesEnglish: Ana said she wanted to have breakfast at the market.

lessons.objectiveFrenchCourseEnglish: Rapporter équitablement deux avis, vérifier les faits auprès de l’hôte et convenir d’un petit-déjeuner.
lessons.settingEnglish: Chamonix guesthouse breakfast before a morning outing
lessons.focusEnglish: Reported speech with a past background: she said she wanted; he said there was not enough time.
lessons.focusFrench: Discours rapporté et imparfait : elle a dit qu’elle voulait ; il disait qu’il n’y avait pas assez de temps.
lessons.teachingNotesEnglish: Lars évoque le mal aigu des montagnes means Lars mentions altitude sickness. Report each friend’s position with a dit que or disait que, then check the pickup time with the host.

passage.titleFrench: Concilier deux amis avant le départ
english: At a guesthouse in Chamonix, Ana and Lars disagree over breakfast before a morning outing.
Ana wants to visit a bakery near the square.
Lars thinks the group should eat at the guesthouse.
Their friend Camille listens to both of them.
Ana says that she wants fresh bread and a walk through town.
Lars says that there may not be enough time before the booked pickup; he also mentions altitude sickness before the mountain outing.
Camille repeats each position without taking sides.
She asks to check the message with the pickup time.
The message says the driver will arrive at the guesthouse at seven thirty.
Camille asks the host when the nearby bakery opens.
The host says it opens at seven, but does not know how long the queue will be.
Camille tells Ana and Lars what the host confirmed and what remains uncertain.
Ana agrees that a queue could make the timing difficult.
Lars says he would still like fresh bread later.
Camille suggests eating the breakfast already offered at the guesthouse.
Camille summarizes the agreement so everyone has the same plan.
They sit down together while the host brings bread and hot drinks.
french: Dans une maison d’hôtes à Chamonix, Ana et Lars ne sont pas d’accord sur le petit-déjeuner avant une sortie matinale.
Ana veut aller dans une boulangerie près de la place.
Lars pense que le groupe devrait manger à la maison d’hôtes.
Leur amie Camille écoute chacun d’eux.
Ana dit qu’elle veut du pain frais et une promenade en ville.
Lars dit qu’il n’y aura peut-être pas assez de temps avant la prise en charge réservée ; il évoque aussi le mal aigu des montagnes avant la sortie en montagne.
Camille reformule chaque point de vue sans prendre parti.
Elle demande à vérifier le message qui indique l’heure de prise en charge.
Le message indique que le chauffeur arrivera à la maison d’hôtes à sept heures et demie.
Camille demande à l’hôte quand ouvre la boulangerie voisine.
L’hôte dit qu’elle ouvre à sept heures, mais ne sait pas combien de temps durera la file d’attente.
Camille dit à Ana et Lars ce que l’hôte a confirmé et ce qui reste incertain.
Ana reconnaît qu’une file d’attente pourrait compliquer l’horaire.
Lars dit qu’il aimerait quand même acheter du pain frais plus tard.
Camille propose de prendre le petit-déjeuner déjà prévu à la maison d’hôtes.
Camille résume l’accord pour que tout le monde suive le même plan.
Ils s’installent ensemble pendant que l’hôte apporte du pain et des boissons chaudes.

lessons.sourceTitleEnglish: Keep a Tired Group Going at a Dawn Lodge Breakfast
lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Encourage a sleepy, cranky group, commit to a clear plan, and keep spirits up while the bread finishes.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: You are the group's organizer, and the AI plays cook Mirta and your sleepy companions Noor, Felipe and Greta: encourage them, commit to tasks with the future (me encargaré, saldremos), and keep spirits up with ¡vamos! and dale while the bread finishes.
lessons.sourceGrammarFocusEnglish: Future for commitments; encouragement register (yo me encargaré del termo; ¡vamos, que saldremos a tiempo!)

sourceWordsEnglish.en: I'll take care of the thermos and the yerba.
Come on, we'll still leave on time!
Felipe, relax, the bread will be ready in a little while.
Mirta, roughly how much longer does the bread need?
Noor, can you put the packed lunches together while we wait?
Greta, I'll make you a mate while the bread bakes.
We'll get to the trail before sunrise, you'll see.
Come on, guys, the day is going to be beautiful.

sourcePassageEnglish: At 5 in the morning, Sam and his companions Noor, Felipe and Greta are having breakfast at a lodge in El Chaltén before heading out to hike.
Mirta, the cook, takes the kettle off the stove and lets them know that the homemade bread needs more time in the oven.
Sam: Mirta, roughly how much longer does the bread need?
Mirta: About 20 minutes, but in the meantime you can eat the pastries with dulce de leche.
Felipe is in a bad mood because he wanted to leave right away, and he says they are going to miss the sunrise.
Sam: Felipe, relax, the bread will be ready in a little while.
Sam: We'll get to the trail before sunrise, you'll see.
Sam calmly explains the plan for the day: they will leave at 6, hike 2 hours to the lagoon and come back to the lodge in the afternoon.
Sam: I'll take care of the thermos and the yerba.
Sam: Noor, can you put the packed lunches together while we wait?
Noor yawns, but she fills each packed lunch with cheese and fruit and leaves room for the bread.
Greta is cold and can't find her jacket or her headlamp.
Felipe, calmer now, tells her: Greta, both things are in your backpack.
Sam: Greta, I'll make you a mate while the bread bakes.
With the hot mate and the pastries, the group's spirits improve a lot.
Mirta takes the homemade bread out of the oven and tells the group: It's ready, guys, the trailhead is a 10-minute walk away.
Sam: Come on, we'll still leave on time!
Sam: Come on, guys, the day is going to be beautiful.

sourceVerbsEnglish.meaningEnglish: to take care of, to be in charge of
sourceVerbsEnglish.exampleEnglish: I take care of the thermos and the yerba.
We leave at 6 with the packed lunches.
We get to the trail before sunrise.
Greta, I'll pour you a mate while we wait for the bread.
We wait for the bread calmly.

sourceGrammarExamplesEnglish: I'll take care of the thermos and you the packed lunches.

lessons.titleFrenchCourseEnglish: Garder le groupe d’accord pendant l’attente
lessons.objectiveFrenchCourseEnglish: Encourager un groupe fatigué, répartir de petites tâches et annoncer un plan réaliste pendant que le pain cuit.

lessons.teachingNotesEnglish: Avoid promising a sunrise or trail arrival; confirm the actual departure and leave route decisions to the group and staff.

passage.titleFrench: Garder le groupe d’accord pendant l’attente
english: At an Alpine refuge, Sam and three friends have an early breakfast.
The cook, Mireille, says the homemade bread needs more time in the oven.
Felipe is tired and wants to leave immediately.
Noor would rather wait for the bread and finish the packed lunches.
Greta asks whether anyone has checked the agreed departure time.
Sam listens, then asks Mireille how much longer the bread needs.
Mireille estimates fifteen minutes, but says she will check the oven again.
Sam says he will take care of the thermos while they wait.
He asks Noor whether she can prepare the packed lunches.
Noor agrees and puts fruit and cheese in each bag.
Greta finds her jacket and headlamp beside her chair.
Sam offers her a cup of herbal tea.
Felipe says he feels less rushed when everyone has a task.
Sam reads the booking message and confirms the agreed departure time.
He avoids promising when they will reach the path.
Mireille checks the bread and brings it to the table.
The group finishes breakfast and checks its plan with the refuge staff.
They leave together after agreeing on the next step.
french: Dans un refuge alpin, Sam et trois amis prennent un petit-déjeuner de bonne heure.
La cuisinière, Mireille, dit que le pain maison doit rester encore au four.
Felipe est fatigué et veut partir tout de suite.
Noor préfère attendre le pain et finir de préparer les pique-niques.
Greta demande si quelqu’un a vérifié l’heure de départ convenue.
Sam écoute, puis demande à Mireille combien de temps il faut encore pour le pain.
Mireille estime qu’il faut quinze minutes, mais dit qu’elle vérifiera encore le four.
Sam dit qu’il s’occupera du thermos pendant l’attente.
Il demande à Noor si elle peut préparer les pique-niques.
Noor accepte et met des fruits et du fromage dans chaque sac.
Greta retrouve sa veste et sa lampe frontale près de sa chaise.
Sam lui propose une tasse de tisane.
Felipe dit qu’il se sent moins pressé quand chacun a une tâche.
Sam lit le message de réservation et confirme l’heure de départ convenue.
Il évite de promettre à quelle heure ils atteindront le sentier.
Mireille vérifie le pain et l’apporte à table.
Le groupe termine son petit-déjeuner et vérifie son programme auprès du personnel du refuge.
Ils partent ensemble après s’être mis d’accord sur la suite.

verbs.exampleEnglish: I will take care of the thermos.
We will leave at the agreed time.
Mireille will check the bread again.
Noor will prepare the packed lunches.
We will wait for the bread without rushing.
verbs.exampleFrench: Nous attendrons le pain sans nous presser.

grammarExamples.french: Je m’occuperai du thermos et tu prépareras les pique-niques.

grammarExamples.english: We will check the departure time before making a promise.
grammarExamples.french: Nous vérifierons l’heure de départ avant de faire une promesse.

lessons.speakingInstructionEnglish: Encourage the group without promising an arrival time; commit to tasks and confirm the booked departure with staff.
lessons.speakingFrench: Je m’occuperai du thermos. Noor, pourrais-tu préparer les pique-niques ? Nous vérifierons l’heure de départ avec Mireille avant de décider.
lessons.regionalNotesEnglish: Alpine refuge services and food availability vary by venue.

lessons.sourceTitleEnglish: Usted or Tú: Coach a Friend at a Casa Particular
lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Explain when to switch between usted and tú, then model it with the host, her grandson and an older guest.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: You are coaching your friend Marcus, and the AI plays Marcus, host señora Odalys, her grandson Yandiel and guest don Rigoberto: explain when to use usted or tú, then model each with softeners like quisiera, ¿me podría…? and ¿te importa…?
lessons.sourceGrammarFocusEnglish: Usted / tú switching; softeners (quisiera, ¿me podría…?, ¿te importa…?)

sourceWordsEnglish.en: Marcus, speak to señora Odalys using usted.
Señora Odalys, could you serve me a little more coffee?
Yandiel, do you mind passing me the papaya?
Don Rigoberto, are you from here, from Trinidad?
I'd like another guava smoothie, if it's no trouble.
You can use tú with Yandiel, because he used tú with us first.
If she tells you to use tú with her, then you switch.
Now you try: ask don Rigoberto for the sugar.

sourcePassageEnglish: Lucía and her friend Marcus are having breakfast on the front porch of a casa particular in Trinidad, Cuba.
The host, señora Odalys, puts a coffee pot of freshly brewed coffee on the table.
Marcus doesn't know which way of addressing people to use with each person at the table, so Lucía explains the difference to him.
Lucía: Marcus, speak to señora Odalys using usted.
Lucía: With the owner of the house or with an older person, usted shows respect.
Lucía: If she tells you to use tú with her, then you switch.
Then Lucía gives an example with a gentle question: Señora Odalys, could you serve me a little more coffee?
Yandiel, the host's grandson, comes out to the porch and asks Marcus: Hey, are you American?
Lucía: You can use tú with Yandiel, because he used tú with us first.
Lucía: Among young people, using tú shows closeness and is not a lack of respect.
Lucía gives the example: Yandiel, do you mind passing me the papaya?
Don Rigoberto, a guest of about 70, comes out of his room and sits down next to Marcus.
Lucía: An older man you call don, you also address with usted.
Marcus asks carefully: Don Rigoberto, are you from here, from Trinidad?
Don Rigoberto smiles and answers: No, I'm from Cienfuegos, but I come to this house every year.
Lucía: Now you try: ask don Rigoberto for the sugar.
Marcus: Don Rigoberto, could you pass me the sugar, please?
At the end, Marcus says to the host with a smile: I'd like another guava smoothie, if it's no trouble.

sourceVerbsEnglish.exampleEnglish: You speak to don Rigoberto using usted.
Yandiel uses tú with us from the very first moment.
Señora Odalys serves the coffee on the front porch.
Ask don Rigoberto for the sugar.

sourceGrammarExamplesEnglish: Señora Odalys, could you pass me the coffee pot, please?
Yandiel, do you mind if I sit here?
lessons.titleFrenchCourseEnglish: Choisir entre vous et tu avec les hôtes
lessons.objectiveFrenchCourseEnglish: Expliquer la différence entre vous et tu, puis adapter les demandes selon la manière dont chaque personne se présente.
lessons.settingEnglish: Québec guesthouse breakfast with a host and fellow guests
lessons.focusEnglish: French vous/tu choice and polite requests: Could you pass the coffee? Do you mind if I sit here?
lessons.focusFrench: Choix entre vous et tu et demandes polies : Pourriez-vous me passer le café ? Ça te dérange si je m’assieds ici ?
lessons.teachingNotesEnglish: French address varies by person, region and relationship; ask or mirror the form offered.

words.fr: la façon de s’adresser à quelqu’un

words.en: Marcus, start by addressing the host with vous.
words.fr: Marcus, commence par vouvoyer notre hôte.

passage.titleFrench: Choisir entre vous et tu avec les hôtes
english: Lucie and Marcus have breakfast at a guesthouse near Québec City.
The host, Madame Lavoie, sets a coffee pot on the table.
Marcus is unsure whether to use tu or vous with each person.
Lucie says that vous is a courteous starting point with someone new.
She adds that people may prefer different forms.
Lucie asks the host: Could you serve me a little more coffee?
Madame Lavoie smiles and says that they may use tu with her.
Marcus thanks her and follows the form she offered.
The host’s grandson, Julien, comes into the room and says hello.
Julien addresses Marcus with tu and asks whether he wants berries.
Marcus asks: Do you mind passing me the berries?
Another guest joins them at the table.
Marcus does not assume that the guest wants tu.
He begins with vous and asks whether the guest is from the area.
The guest answers and introduces himself as Émile.
Lucie reminds Marcus that he can ask when he is unsure.
Marcus asks Émile politely to pass the sugar.
At the end, he asks the host for another apple juice.
french: Lucie et Marcus prennent le petit-déjeuner dans une maison d’hôtes près de Québec.
L’hôte, madame Lavoie, pose une cafetière sur la table.
Marcus ne sait pas s’il doit dire tu ou vous à chaque personne.
Lucie dit que vous est un point de départ courtois avec une personne que l’on ne connaît pas.
Elle ajoute que les gens peuvent préférer des formes différentes.
Lucie demande à l’hôte : « Pourriez-vous me servir encore un peu de café ? »
Madame Lavoie sourit et dit qu’ils peuvent la tutoyer.
Marcus la remercie et adopte la forme qu’elle a proposée.
Le petit-fils de l’hôte, Julien, entre dans la pièce et dit bonjour.
Julien tutoie Marcus et lui demande s’il veut des petits fruits.
Marcus demande : « Ça te dérange de me passer les petits fruits ? »
Un autre client les rejoint à table.
Marcus ne suppose pas que le client souhaite être tutoyé.
Il commence par vous et demande au client s’il est de la région.
Le client répond et se présente : il s’appelle Émile.
Lucie rappelle à Marcus qu’il peut poser la question s’il hésite.
Marcus demande poliment à Émile de lui passer le sucre.
À la fin, il demande à l’hôte encore un jus de pomme.

verbs.exampleEnglish: Marcus speaks to the host using vous at first.
verbs.exampleFrench: Marcus parle d’abord à l’hôte en la vouvoyant.

verbs.exampleEnglish: The host serves coffee at breakfast.
verbs.exampleFrench: L’hôte sert du café au petit-déjeuner.

verbs.exampleEnglish: Marcus asks whether he may use tu.
verbs.exampleFrench: Marcus demande s’il peut tutoyer son interlocuteur.

verbs.exampleEnglish: Julien passes the berries to Marcus.
verbs.exampleFrench: Julien passe les petits fruits à Marcus.

grammarExamples.english: Could you pass me the coffee pot, please?
grammarExamples.french: Pourriez-vous me passer la cafetière, s’il vous plaît ?

grammarExamples.english: Do you mind if I sit here?
grammarExamples.french: Ça te dérange si je m’assieds ici ?

lessons.speakingInstructionEnglish: Coach Marcus on vous and tu, model two polite requests, and explain that he can ask rather than assume a preference.
lessons.speakingFrench: Avec une personne que tu ne connais pas, commence par vous. Si elle te propose de la tutoyer, tu peux changer. Pourriez-vous me passer la cafetière, s’il vous plaît ?
lessons.regionalNotesEnglish: Québec tutoiement and vouvoiement vary by speaker and context.
